newsitem.title: CHINA: U.S. wants a slice of new Shanghai airport.
newsitem.headline: U.S. wants a slice of new Shanghai airport.

text.p: Shanghai city officials have been asked to consider U.S. companies when awarding major infrastructure and development projects in the city worth more than $1 billion, a senior U.S. official said on Thursday.
Undersecretary of Commerce Stuart Eizenstat said he had presented Shanghai officials with a list of projects "for which we thought U.S. companies were competitive", he said.
These included telecommunications and energy developments in Shanghai's premier development zone of Pudong, and the zone's international airport, Eizenstat told reporters.
"We estimate China will spend $700 billion in the next five years in developing infrastructure," Eizenstat said.

He said that in presenting a specific list of projects to officials of the Pudong New Area he was not demanding that U.S. companies be awarded an arbitrary share in order to help balance Beijing's $39.5 billion trade deficit with Washington.
Washington's trade deficit with Beijing grew in 1996 by $6 billion, as imports from China soared while U.S. exports to China remained fairly static.
Promoting U.S. companies as participants in China's massive infrastrucutural overhaul was an effort to redress the trade imbalance, Eizenstat said.
He said he believed that U.S. companies would win their fair share of the projects if the contracts were awarded equitably.
"If there is a fair and transparent procurement process for these projects, we will win our fair share," he said.
This would go some way to reducing the trade deficit, he said, adding that Beijing put the deficit at $10 billion.
The Pudong airport is one of 32 airport projects in China's current five-year plan totalling around $5 billion.
Pudong's airport, 30 km (18.6 miles) east of the city, is due to open in 2000 with a single runway and terminal capacity of 20 million passengers.
The $1.5 billion Phase 1 will provide nose gates for 34 aircraft, with subsequent phases involving three more parallel runways and three more terminals, according to press reports.

Shanghai's existing Hongqiao international airport is 15 km (9.3 miles) from the city and is reportedly close to its current capcity of 11 million passengers a year, with expansion planned to increase it to 13 million, the reports said.
